label: Takarkori Late Pastoral winter camp, 3000 BC

location.modernLabel: Takarkori rock shelter, Tadrart Acacus, southwest Libya
location.coordinateMeaning: The same rock-shelter and wadi locality used by SAH-9000 and SAH-6000.

temporal.localTimeInput: 08:00 local hour, calendar day and season unspecified
temporal.supportedResolution: Approximately 4.95 ka cal BP, within Late Pastoral LP1 at 5.9 to 4.3 ka cal BP or 3950 to 2350 BC.
temporal.precisionBoundary: The phase supports brief winter camps and specialized herding, not an exact day, herd count, water level, camp layout, or named group.

habitation.evidence: LP1 is associated with brief winter camps of nomadic specialized herders, with sheep and goat emphasis and a directly supported pen area.
habitation.qualification: Sparse seasonal camp use is defensible; permanent village life and dense occupation are not.

viewpoint.support: Rock-shelter floor, trampled camp ground, or wadi sediment near the supported pen area.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The requested date falls within Late Pastoral LP1, associated with brief winter camps of specialized nomadic herders.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: A few herders and a compact seasonal work scene replace permanent settlement.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: An animal-pen area, trampled ground, and thick hardened ovicaprine dung directly characterize the late sequence.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: Sheep or goat movement, compressed dusty ground, pen material, and dung carry the phase through ordinary pastoral work.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: Water availability declined and became more seasonal, while local and regional water persisted variably.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: An aridifying grass-shrub and rock system with reduced seasonal water replaces the earlier humid abundance without collapsing into a guaranteed waterless modern desert.

obligations: Make the scene a sparse seasonal pastoral camp rather than a village.
Use sheep or goat work, pen wear, trampled ground, and dung as phase-bearing material.
Show an aridifying, more open and seasonal water system while preserving uncertainty about exact local water.
Keep the same morning shelter optic used by the earlier cards.
oracleOnlyContradictions: Dense permanent settlement exceeds the Late Pastoral camp evidence.
A vast cattle-centred dairying tableau is not the directly supported LP1 emphasis.
A universally waterless modern desert overstates the local chronology.
Exact herd size, camp plan, and water level are unresolved.

sources.title: Aquatic fauna from Takarkori reveals Holocene central Saharan climate and palaeohydrography
supports: declining fish proportion and water availability

sources.title: Bayesian chronology of the Takarkori archaeological sequence
Takarkori palaeoenvironment and Holocene cultural sequence

uncertainty: Exact local water body, season, rainfall, vegetation density, and weather.
Camp layout, herd size, garments, tools, and named group at the unspecified day.
The calibrated phase ranges are maximum spans and can overlap statistically.

review.notes: LP1 chronology, seasonal camp character, pen material, ovicaprine emphasis, and aridification are source-checked; exact scene detail remains bounded inference.
